prompt.en: A designer wants to increase a 22 µF timing capacitance using another identical capacitor. Which connection gives the larger total?

text.en: Series, because capacitances add end-to-end like resistances.

feedback.en: Series capacitors follow the reciprocal rule. Equal series capacitors give a smaller total.

text.en: Either connection, because identical parts leave the value unchanged.

feedback.en: The connection changes the total even when the individual parts are identical.

text.en: Parallel, because both capacitors store charge across the same voltage.

feedback.en: Parallel capacitances add, giving 44 µF here.

text.en: Series, because the total is the product of the two labels.

feedback.en: Multiplying capacitance labels alone is not a valid series combination rule.

explanation.en: Capacitor connection rules are opposite to the simple resistor combination pattern.

prompt.en: An ideal coil and capacitor are tested separately as frequency rises. Which pair of trends should guide an RF bypass design?

text.en: Coil opposition rises; capacitor opposition falls.

feedback.en: Inductive reactance rises with frequency, while capacitive reactance falls.

text.en: Both oppositions rise because faster AC always meets more opposition.

feedback.en: That trend fits the coil, but capacitive reactance falls as frequency rises.

text.en: Both oppositions fall because RF passes through every reactive part easily.

feedback.en: The capacitor's reactance falls, but the coil's rises.

text.en: Coil opposition falls; capacitor opposition rises.

feedback.en: Those trends are reversed. They would lead to choosing the wrong RF path.

explanation.en: An RF choke impedes unwanted RF in series; a suitable bypass capacitor gives it an easier shunt path.

prompt.en: A series tuned circuit is at resonance. Its capacitance is then increased while the source frequency stays fixed. What happens?

text.en: It remains exactly resonant because the resistance stayed the same.

feedback.en: Resistance affects losses and sharpness. L and C set the ideal resonant frequency.

text.en: Its resonant frequency falls, so the source is now above resonance.

feedback.en: More capacitance lowers the resonant frequency; the unchanged source now lies above it.

text.en: Its resonant frequency rises, so the source is now below resonance.

feedback.en: More capacitance lowers, rather than raises, the resonant frequency.

text.en: It becomes a parallel resonant circuit because its impedance rises.

feedback.en: Changing a value does not change the series connection into parallel branches.

explanation.en: Resonance is a frequency condition as well as a circuit arrangement. Changing C moves that condition.
